name: python-vacasa-connect-sdk
what_it_holds: Official-looking Python SDK published under the Vacasa GitHub org for the connect.vacasa.com API (units/properties, reviews, generic GET endpoints). Confirmed via README: requires OIDC client-id/secret/scope credentials tied to a Vacasa owner/partner account — this is private property-management data, not a public dataset. 1 star, updated 2026-07-22 (actively maintained).
why_useful: Confirms Vacasa's API surface (units, reviews) exists and is documented, useful if the team ever gets partner/owner access, but as-is it cannot be pulled without credentials, so it does not satisfy the 'public source' cataloguing bar.
time_coverage: n/a — live API, no historical archive implied
license: MIT (code license; underlying API access is gated separately)

name: vacasa-ha
what_it_holds: Home Assistant custom integration exposing a Vacasa owner's own booking calendar and sensors (occupied/vacant, upcoming bookings) inside a smart-home dashboard. Requires the user's own Vacasa owner login; single-property scope by design, not a market-wide dataset. Updated 2026-07-08.
why_useful: Shows Vacasa exposes a booking-calendar API per property, but scope is one owner's one property at a time and needs credentials — not usable as a market-level dataset.
themes: Hostelworld, Hipcamp, Outdoorsy, RVshare, Sonder, Vacasa, Inspirato, Marriott Homes & Villas, Plum Guide, onefinestay, Flatio, Blueground datasets or filings parsers

name: MaurizioFD/recsys-challenge-2019-trivago
what_it_holds: Politecnico di Milano team's full solution code/notebooks for the RecSys Challenge 2019 (Policloud8), including preprocessing scripts that read the trivago dataset (train.csv/test.csv/item_metadata.csv style files) in full/local/small (100k-row) modes. No raw data committed (dataset must still be obtained from trivago), but the preprocessing code documents the exact schema (impression lists + parallel price lists per clickout, per-country feature importance table referencing UK/US/DE/FR/IT etc.).
why_useful: Turns the trivago metasearch dataset into something immediately usable — schema, cleaning, feature engineering already written — if the team decides to pull the underlying trivago data as an ex-Airbnb hotel-pricing comparator.
geography: Europe + a handful of other trivago markets
themes: Google Hotel Ads / Google Travel price datasets and scrapers; hotel metasearch price panels
why_all: Turns the trivago metasearch dataset into something immediately usable — schema, cleaning, feature engineering already written — if the team decides to pull the underlying trivago data as an ex-Airbnb hotel-pricing comparator.

name: google/hotel-ads-etl-tool
what_it_holds: Official (but explicitly deprecated/unmaintained) Google repo: a Python + Apache Beam/Dataflow ETL pipeline that pulls 'Hotel Ads API Reports' (Google Hotel Ads performance data: impressions, clicks, bookings by property) into BigQuery. Requires OAuth2 credentials tied to an active Google Hotel Ads / Hotel Center partner account plus a GCP project (Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Dataflow enabled). 9 stars, 7 forks, Python 93.9%/Shell 6.1%.
why_useful: The most directly on-theme repo found (literally 'hotel ads etl'), and shows what fields the Hotel Ads API historically exposed, but it is gated behind a partner-only Google Hotel Ads account (a hotel/OTA advertiser login), which the team does not have and which is out of scope to acquire. Useful mainly as documentation of what a real Google Hotel Ads price/bid panel looks like, not as a pullable public dataset.
